title: Doubly Robust AUC Optimization against Noisy and Adversarial Samples

problem.claim: Adversarial and noisy samples threaten the performance of learning models, including in AUC optimization settings.

gap.claim: Existing defenses address adversarial and noisy samples separately, and the authors report no AUC-optimization method that secures against both simultaneously.

contributions.claim: Proposes a doubly robust dAUC optimization algorithm called DRAUC.
Integrates self-paced learning and adversarial training under AUC optimization and provides a statistical upper bound to AUC adversarial risk.
Defines an optimization objective and an efficient alternatively stochastic descent algorithm motivated by the statistical upper bound.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe DRAUC as a novel doubly robust dAUC optimization algorithm.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On several standard datasets, the authors report that DRAUC has better noise robustness and adversarial robustness than state-of-the-art algorithms.

narrative_sequence.summary: AUC is important and widely used, especially for imbalanced datasets.
Noisy and adversarial samples threaten learning-model performance, while existing defenses treat them separately.
The authors identify a lack of AUC-optimization defenses against both harmful sample types simultaneously.
DRAUC combines self-paced learning, adversarial training, a statistical risk bound, and an alternatively stochastic descent algorithm.
Experiments on several standard datasets are reported to show improved noise and adversarial robustness over state-of-the-art algorithms.

source_observation.claim: The proposed method combines defenses for noisy and adversarial samples within an AUC-optimization framework.

interpretation.claim: A unified objective may address interacting data-quality and attack threats more directly than separate defenses.

application.claim: For imbalanced-classification systems exposed to both corrupted and adversarial data, consider jointly modeling robustness threats during AUC optimization.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish which threat combinations, datasets, or deployment conditions determine when the unified approach is preferable.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the noise and adversarial threat models.
The abstract does not provide dataset names, quantitative results, or experimental protocols.
The abstract does not describe the optimization objective, algorithm complexity, or statistical bound in detail.
